description: Every stage an analysis run passes through, in order, plus the run modes and the one gate that matters. Generates the stage enumeration, the resume logic and the status screens.

principles.nothingWritesToThePlatform: No stage writes to a Power Platform environment in any mode. There is no flag that changes this, because the value of a discovery that is safe to run in a first meeting exceeds anything a write would add.
principles.publishIsTheOnlyWrite: The publish stage writes work items to Azure DevOps and is the only stage in the product that writes anywhere outside its own database. It sits behind an approval recorded against a named person and the exact backlog they saw.
principles.approvalBindsToAHash: The approval records a hash of the backlog as it was presented. A backlog that changes afterwards no longer matches and the publish refuses. Approving one thing and publishing another is the failure this exists to prevent.
principles.resumable: Every stage checkpoints. A run that dies during extraction resumes rather than restarting, because re-extracting a large estate costs an hour and re-running a checker job costs a queue place.
principles.idempotentPublish: Publishing twice creates no duplicates. Every work item carries a deterministic key derived from the engagement, the rule and the component, and an existing item is updated rather than added.

modes.name: Quick scan
modes.purpose: Counts, the low code ratio, lifecycle findings and the top of the debt list. Fifteen minutes, no checker job, no model estimates. The mode for the meeting where somebody asks how bad it is.

modes.name: Assessment
modes.purpose: The full rule set, the checker, model estimates with rationale, the report and the backlog. The deliverable for a paid discovery.

modes.name: Publish to Azure DevOps
modes.purpose: Writes the approved backlog into a project as work items. The only mode that writes anything to a client system.
modes.note: Runs against an existing assessment rather than re-analysing. Re-analysing here would mean the thing published is not the thing approved.

modes.name: Compare
modes.purpose: This run against a previous one. What was fixed, what appeared, what moved. The mode that makes a second engagement worth buying.

stages.name: Check connections
stages.description: Authenticates every configured source and reports the identity it authenticated as, what it is allowed to read, and which evidence sources are therefore reachable. A connection that succeeds with too few privileges fails later in a way that looks exactly like an estate with nothing in it.

stages.name: Select solutions
stages.description: Lists the solutions in the environment with their component counts, managed state, publisher and version, and records which were chosen. A run always states what it looked at, because a report covering four of nineteen solutions and a report covering all nineteen look identical on the cover page.

stages.name: Extract
stages.description: Reads components from every reachable source into staging, uninterpreted. Each entity read is recorded separately with its own success or failure, so a partial read is visibly partial rather than arithmetically invisible.
stages.partialFailureBehaviour: A run continues when some entities fail and marks every rule depending on them as not assessed. A run where more than a quarter of entities failed stops, because at that point the report would describe an environment nobody read.

stages.name: Run the Power Apps checker
stages.description: Uploads the solution to the checker service, polls for completion and downloads the report. Long running: a minute at best and five or more on a large solution.

stages.name: Normalise
stages.description: Staged records become components in the model declared by component-model.json, with craft and lifecycle attached. Normalising twice updates rather than duplicating, so a mapping defect is fixed and replayed without going back to the client's environment for the data again.

stages.name: Resolve references
stages.description: Builds the dependency graph: which form loads which script, which flow uses which connection reference, which column appears on nothing. Most of the interesting rules need this and none of them can run before it.

stages.name: Apply the rules
stages.description: Every rule in the catalogue against every component in scope, plus the checker results folded in. Produces findings with evidence attached. A rule whose evidence source was unreachable produces a not assessed record rather than nothing.

stages.name: Estimate
stages.description: One model call per finding, with the band as an anchor and the engagement override table consulted first. Rationale required on every estimate. Falls back to the band when no model is configured and says so in the report.
stages.orderNote: Before score, not after it. The score stage is what persists the findings, and the estimator is what attaches an estimate to each one, so scoring first saves every finding with no estimate on it. This contract declared the other order for months while the worker ran this one, and nothing noticed because nothing held the two together.

stages.name: Score
stages.description: The low code ratio, the debt profile per domain, the lifecycle position and the comparison against a previous run where one exists. Every number carries its own definition into the export.

stages.name: Build the backlog
stages.description: Findings grouped into work items per devops-mapping.json, with acceptance criteria and test requirements written per rule. Produces the hash the approval binds to.

stages.name: Approval
stages.description: A named person approves the backlog they are looking at. Not a setting and not a configuration flag: a row, inserted, recording who and when and which hash.

stages.name: Publish to Azure DevOps
stages.description: Creates or updates work items in the configured project. Refuses without a matching approval. Records every item created with its identifier, so a publish can be reported on and, if it was wrong, found again.

stages.name: Export
stages.description: The report as PDF, the findings and backlog as Excel. Produced from the stored run rather than recomputed, so the document and the screen agree.

deliverables.name: Assessment report
deliverables.description: The document a client reads. Findings, the ratio, the debt profile, the modernisation options and the estimate with its assumptions.

deliverables.name: Findings
deliverables.description: Every finding, one row each, with component, rule, severity, evidence, estimate range, rationale and confidence. The sheet that gets filtered in a workshop.

deliverables.name: Backlog
deliverables.description: The work items as they would be created, with acceptance criteria and points. Exported whether or not anybody publishes to DevOps.

deliverables.name: Component inventory
deliverables.description: Everything found, by type and solution, with craft and lifecycle. The appendix nobody reads and everybody asks for.

deliverables.name: Comparison
deliverables.description: This run against a previous one.

checks.name: Environment health
checks.description: What the identity can actually read, which evidence sources are therefore reachable, and the privileges it holds. Part of connect, reported separately.
checks.whenOff: The run proceeds on whatever the credential happens to reach, and a source that is unreachable is indistinguishable from one that is empty.

checks.name: Solution checker
checks.description: Microsoft's own static analysis, submitted as a job on their side and waited for.
checks.cost: The slowest part of a run by a wide margin, and the usual reason an assessment takes hours rather than minutes.
checks.whenOff: Every rule whose evidence is a checker result is reported as not assessed, never as passing.

checks.name: Model estimates
checks.description: Per component estimates with a rationale, rather than the band default for the component type.
checks.whenOff: Estimates fall back to band defaults, which is what a quick scan does. The report says which of the two it used.

checks.name: Export the chosen solutions
checks.description: Asks the environment for each chosen solution as a zip, through the same call a person makes when they click Export, and reads it as though it had been uploaded.
checks.cost: Around a minute per solution against a real environment, so a dozen is a quarter of an hour. Nothing is written to the environment: an export is a read.
checks.whenOff: The fourteen rules that read a solution file and the three that need the checker are reported as not assessed. A live connection is then no richer than a metadata read.

solutionSelection.description: A run lists what the environment holds, stops, and waits for somebody to say what it should read. The pause is a run status rather than a second run, so one discovery is one row and one timeline.
solutionSelection.whyNotEverything: Most of what a Dataverse environment contains is Microsoft's own first party solutions. Reading them costs the longest part of a run and produces a report about Dynamics rather than about the client's work.
solutionSelection.whyNotSilently: A report covering four of nineteen solutions and a report covering all nineteen look identical on the cover page. Every solution found is recorded whether or not it was chosen, so the run can always say what it did not look at.

firstParty.description: How a solution is judged to be Microsoft's rather than the client's. Deliberately generous in what it treats as first party and conservative about the consequence, which is only that a box starts unticked and somebody can tick it.
firstParty.note: A judgement, not a fact the platform states. The prefix is the strongest signal because a publisher name can be renamed and a solution cannot change the prefix its components carry.
